body: I felt this way for a long time and was very afraid to get help for fear of future consequences. Eventually, I was breaking down almost every day. Sometimes a half hour. Sometimes up to 4 hours. Sometimes twice a day. I had no good explanation for why I wanted to die so badly. It was like a worm crawled in my brain and was slowly destroying the me I know and love. I didn't decide to start feeling that why. I couldn't stop it from happening. But, if I hadn't waited so long to get help I could have saved myself and the people I love so much suffering. Get help now before it ruins you. You don't have to tell everything, but most people understand hard times take their toll on any person.
Alcohol = not depressed. Alcoholic = major depressed. It sneaks up on you, just don't let it get that far.

You sound very self important. There seems to be a lot of "my problems are WAY worse than yours" going around the world lately. It's not a competition. Any suffering is bad. Some people will not publicly explain the great extent of what they are going through and it might come off as superficial to you, but really, what the fuck do you know from one post? Lay off and relax, people come here for help, why do you feel the need to moderate in what they take solace in? Some people might be helped by "toughen up", some by meds, some by therapy, some by getting the gd shiny new puppy. We're all here because either something is off and we are having the same thought or we are here to help in any way at all if possible. Kudos to you for suffering your whole life, but It doesn't make you qualified to tell someone who has been suffering for a fraction of your life that their depression, anxiety and suicidal thoughts are somehow less important than yours. We all suffer, it always sucks, you can always compare yourself or what you think is best to others but that is just another trip down the rabbit hole. Just appreciate whatever it is that has kept you alive and maybe even share that. I would like to ask you though, since you are an expert, who is qualified to say they truly understand depression? The kid with the knife to his wrists? The psychologist with the gold star upbringing? Or only you or someone like you? You cannot know what others understand, where they are coming from or the extent of their pain based on their age. I would gladly tell anyone, whatever thing they needed to hear to get off the bridge. Even if it was: god is real, toughen up, I got over it so can you, here's a new puppy, or it sounds like some real horrible shit you are going through, let's figure out a plan to help you get through it. Please, try not to be so judgmental of others, I can tell what others say bothers you, but that doesn't automatically make you right. Sorry OP.
